author: NASASpaceflight
description:
China surprised the spaceflight community this week with the debut launch of a brand-new rocket that appeared to fly without the usual public hazard notices that observers rely on. Was it dangerous, or simply a different approach to launch operations?

In this week's This Week in Spaceflight, we break down what happened with China's unexpected Chang Zheng 12B launch, why it caught trackers off guard, and what it means for the country's rapidly expanding reusable rocket ambitions.

We also cover Blue Origin's plans to return New Glenn to flight before the end of the year, The Exploration Company's successful Nyx capsule drop test and teaser for its future heavy-lift launcher, Rocket Lab's latest Neutron milestone, ULA's first 85K Centaur, NASA's Commercial LEO Destination reversal, Artemis III preparations, and much more.

🚀 Stories this week:
• China's surprise Chang Zheng 12B launch
• Blue Origin's return-to-flight plans
• The Exploration Company's Nyx capsule tests
• Rocket Lab Neut
title: China Launched a Rocket Without Warning. | This Week in Spaceflight
